festivals: Sunderkand Path and Hanuman Chalisa recitations on Tuesdays and Saturdays

history.period: 1754 CE (Vikram Samvat 1811; founding date disputed - see summary)
history.summary: One of India's most famous Hanuman temples, founded by the devotee Mohandas Ji Maharaj after a Jat farmer of Asota village (Nagaur district) unearthed a swayambhu Hanuman idol while ploughing in 1754 (Shravan Shukla Navami); that night both the Thakur of Asota and Mohandas Ji dreamt of Hanuman instructing them to install the idol at Salasar. Uniquely, the idol shows Hanuman with a round human-like face, beard and moustache (Dadhi-Munch wale Balaji). FLAG: the official temple site dates construction to 1759 (Samvat 1815), not 1754; Mohandas Ji's samadhi is dated 1850 (Vaishakh Shukla Triyodashi) on the official site but 1794 (VS 1851) on other pages - dates vary across sources. The Akhand Dhuni (eternal fire) lit by Mohandas Ji and the coconut-tying vow tradition are central. Temple first built in mudstone by Mohandas Ji, rebuilt by Rao Devi Singh of Sikar, later developed by his descendants Kaniram and Ishwardas. NOTE: CSV town Salasar is in Churu district, not a district town itself - district flagged as Churu.

name: Salasar Balaji Temple
town_description: Salasar is a pilgrim town in Sujangarh tehsil of Churu district, Rajasthan, on the Jaipur-Bikaner National Highway 65. The town's identity and economy revolve around the Balaji temple, with dozens of guest houses and dharamshalas serving pilgrims year-round.
tradition: Vaishnavite (Hanuman devotion; folk worship with Savamani and coconut-tying traditions)

travel.railway: Sujangarh (~24 km, verify); Sikar (~57 km, verify)
travel.road: On NH 65 (Jaipur-Bikaner highway); buses and taxis from Jaipur, Sikar and Sujangarh

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Chaitra Purnima and Sharad Purnima fairs draw millions
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily; Mangla aarti ~4:00 AM to night aarti ~10:00 PM (schedules vary across sources - verify locally)
